description: A 3-pin SPDT (single-pole double-throw) switch: pin 2 (common) is always connected to either pin 1 or pin 3, depending on the handle position.
how_to_use: Pin 2 is the common terminal, always live. Pins 1 and 3 are the two throw positions — NOT a harmless swap like a resistor's legs: swapping which one is wired changes which handle position reads active, so this isn't treated as symmetric. Many uses only wire one of pin 1/pin 3 plus pin 2, leaving the other throw position unconnected.
